source_of_truth: Operator design conclusion (2026-06-02) plus code verification at HEAD c814cc9: DontPanic must be a local control plane that both humans and interactive agents operate from one shared state. ActionItem (operator_console.py:174), RenderedEvent (event_copy.py:78), and ActionChoice (operations_guidance.py:154) already triangulate into one contract via tested projections; this plan formalizes ActionItem as canonical, adds the human-facing control-plane fields, classifies harnesses honestly, and proves renderer parity — explicitly excluding orchestration-tree governance (Plan B) and the plan-quality recast (2026-06-01-001).

user_journeys.name: one-action-three-surfaces
user_journeys.description: An operational blocker (gate, capability gap, operations recommendation, or event) is produced once and rendered consistently to a human (dashboard card), an interactive agent (CLI/JSON what-now), and an onboarding agent (agent-brief managed block) — the same action, deduped once, never recomputed per surface.
acceptance_signals: same action matched by dedupe_key across all three renderers
deduped to one occurrence per response
secret-shaped substrings scrubbed at the render boundary

user_journeys.name: honest-agent-role
user_journeys.description: An interactive agent (or human) inspecting agent status sees three independent capabilities — can it operate DontPanic, can it be dispatched as a worker, can it orchestrate sub-agents — instead of a single mutually-exclusive role, so an unsupported operator (Grok) is told it can operate but not be dispatched, and a fan-out-capable harness is reported honestly without yet being governed.
acceptance_signals: three independent capability booleans in agent status --json
Grok reports can_operate=true, can_be_dispatched=false with operate-but-not-dispatch brief wording
can_orchestrate is reported, not acted on (no tree governance)

user_journeys.name: honest-command-safety
user_journeys.description: Every action that carries a command has had that command validated at the ActionItem boundary, so no surface ever renders an unvalidated or unsafe exact_command, and command safety is expressed by exact_command + automatable rather than a redundant safe_command field.
acceptance_signals: ActionItem rejects an unvalidated exact_command at construction
no safe_command field is added to ActionItem / the control-plane spine (pre-existing safe_command in config_inventory.py and skill_recommendation.py is out of scope and left untouched)

non_goals: Orchestration-tree governance: tree-aware budget/breaker rollup, multi-writer checkpoint/undo, multi-writer drift (deferred to a demand-gated Plan B).
The native desktop app-wrapper that owns the local-server lifecycle.
Editing the locked flat operator/worker objective_contract of 2026-05-30-001 in place.

Adding a safe_command field to ActionItem — command safety stays exact_command + automatable. Pre-existing safe_command usage in config_inventory.py and skill_recommendation.py is a separate contract, out of scope, and not migrated here.
